components.name: accordion-panel
components.description: A section that opens and closes, on the native <details>: the browser does the keyboard (Enter and Space on the heading), the find-in-page opening and the announcements. Panels with the same `group` form an accordion where one is open at a time (<details name>). `open` is two-way.

components.name: auto-grid
components.description: A grid with as many equal columns as fit, each at least `min` wide: four on a wide screen, one on a phone, with no media queries.

components.name: chat-message
components.description: One message: avatar, author, time, text (with @mentions and links picked out), the message it replies to, and reactions. `me` is the signed-in user's name: their messages, mentions of them and their reactions are marked.

components.name: choice-cards
components.description: Pick one of several cards: a radio group. A form control; arrow keys move the choice. Each item is `{ id, title, detail, price, note }` (`note` and `price` optional).

components.name: cluster-layout
components.description: Children in a row that wraps onto more lines when there isn't room: buttons, tags, footer links. `justify` and `align` line them up.

components.name: color-swatches
components.description: Pick a colour from `colors`. A form control (a radio group): arrow keys move the choice.

components.name: combo-box
components.description: A combobox: type to filter, arrow keys to move, Enter to pick, Escape to close. A form control. `items` is `[{ value, label }]`; `value` is two-way.

components.name: dashboard-shell
components.description: An app's frame: a sidebar of sections, a top bar with the page title and a user menu, and the page in the middle. In a narrow space it folds the sidebar behind a Menu button, measuring itself rather than the screen.

components.name: date-range
components.description: A check-in and check-out date, as one value `{ start, end }` ("YYYY-MM-DD" strings). A form control: invalid until both are set and `end` is after `start`.

components.name: donut-chart
components.description: A donut chart of `segments` (`[{ label, value, tone }]`, `tone` 0–7), with the total in the middle and a legend. Choosing a segment (or its legend entry) selects it; again clears it.

components.name: dropdown-menu
components.description: A menu of actions behind a button, on the platform's `popover`: the browser puts it in the top layer and closes it on Escape or a click outside. Down or Up on the button opens it; arrow keys, Home, End and typing a letter move among the items; Enter or Space picks one, and focus goes back to the button. It's placed below the button by CSS anchor positioning, or by script where that isn't supported. `items` is `[{ value, label, disabled? }]`.

components.name: flip-card
components.description: A card with two faces that flips in 3D. Click, Space or Enter flips it. Shadow DOM: the faces are slotted, and the page's CSS styles them, not the card's.

components.name: image-gallery
components.description: A photo gallery: a masonry grid in reading order and a lightbox with previous and next (arrow keys too). Photos come from `items`, or from `src`, a gallery.json that `npx zubra-imager <photos>` writes (sizes in AVIF, WebP and JPEG, alt text, placeholders). `index` is the open photo (-1 when closed) and is two-way.

components.name: kanban-column
components.description: A board column: a heading with a count and an optional work-in-progress limit, its cards (the default slot) and a drop zone for cards dragged from anywhere on the board.

components.name: line-chart
components.description: A price chart: an area under a line, with the high, low and a crosshair that follows the pointer and shows the value under it.

components.name: masonry-grid
components.description: A masonry layout for any items of different heights (cards, notes, photos): packed into columns as wide as `column` allows, while the order stays the reading order, so Tab, screen readers and search see the items left to right, top to bottom, as written. Browsers with native masonry (CSS grid lanes) lay it out themselves; the others get a small script that measures each item.

components.name: message-composer
components.description: Writing a message: Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, the box grows with the text, an emoji menu inserts at the caret, and a message being replied to shows above.

components.name: modal-dialog
components.description: A modal dialog on the native <dialog>: the page behind is inert, focus moves into the dialog and back to where it was, and Escape, the close button or a click on the backdrop closes it. `open` is two-way.

components.name: money-input
components.description: An amount of money. Typing is free-form; on blur it's formatted (`1234.5` → `1,234.50`). The value is a number (or null when empty). A form control: `required` and `min` validate it.

components.name: pricing-block
components.description: Pricing plans side by side, with a monthly or yearly switch, a featured plan, and what each includes. Choosing a plan fires `choose` with the plan and period.

components.name: progress-ring
components.description: A ring that fills to `value` of `max`, with what's in the middle from the default slot (the percentage if empty).

components.name: quantity-stepper
components.description: A number with − and + buttons, between `min` and `max`. A form control.

components.name: segmented-control
components.description: A row of mutually exclusive options. `options` is `[{ value, label }]`.

components.name: settings-block
components.description: An account settings page: profile, notification switches, light or dark appearance, and a delete that asks first. `value` holds it all and is two-way; Save fires `save`.

components.name: sidebar-layout
components.description: A sidebar beside the main content that moves above it when the content would get too narrow (`content-min`), with no media queries, so it works in any container.

components.name: signin-block
components.description: A sign-in form: email, password with show and hide, keep me signed in, reset and sign-up links, and an error that's announced. Submitting fires `signin`; with an `action` it also posts as a plain form.

components.name: spark-line
components.description: A small line of recent values, green when it ends higher than it started, red when lower.

components.name: stack-layout
components.description: Children one above the other with the same `gap` between them: the vertical rhythm of a page, a form or a card.

components.name: star-rating
components.description: A star rating that is a form control: it submits its value under its `name`, is invalid while `required` and unset, and goes back to 0 when its form resets. `readonly` shows a rating.

components.name: step-indicator
components.description: Where a multi-step flow is: steps done (which can be revisited), the current one, and those ahead.

components.name: streak-grid
components.description: A habit's last weeks as a grid of days (a column per week, Monday at the top), shaded by how much of the goal was done. Choosing a day toggles it; arrow keys move between days. `log` maps "YYYY-MM-DD" to a count; `today` is "YYYY-MM-DD".

components.name: tab-list
components.description: Tabs: a tab list and the panels it switches between. The panels are the slotted elements with a `data-tab` attribute matching a tab's value; they get role=tabpanel, are labelled by their tab, and are hidden unless chosen. Arrow keys, Home and End move between the tabs (one tab stop), and the focused tab is chosen as it moves, unless `manual`, where Enter or Space chooses it. `tabs` is `[{ value, label }]`; `value` is two-way and defaults to the first tab.

components.name: tag-input
components.description: A list of tags you type: Enter or comma adds one, Backspace in the empty field removes the last, × removes any. Suggestions come from `suggestions`. A form control.

components.name: toggle-switch
components.description: An on/off switch with a label and a description. A form control (submits "on" when checked).

components.name: tool-tip
components.description: A short description shown when its trigger is hovered or focused: the trigger is the slotted element, and the tip describes it (aria-describedby), so a screen reader reads it with the trigger's name. It shows after `delay` milliseconds, stays while the pointer is over it, and Escape hides it without moving focus (WCAG 1.4.13). It sits in the top layer (`popover`), placed above the trigger by CSS anchor positioning, or by script where that isn't supported.

components.name: action-button
components.description: A button in six variants and three sizes, on a native <button> (or <a> with `href`), so it submits forms, takes `type`, and works with the keyboard and screen readers as the browser's own. `loading` keeps its size, shows a spinner, marks it busy and stops it being pressed again.

components.name: text-field
components.description: A labelled text field on a native <input> (or <textarea> with `rows`), so it submits under its `name`, autofills, and validates as the browser's own (`required`, `type="email"`, `minlength`, `pattern`). The message shows after the field is left, or when the form is submitted, and is linked to the field for screen readers. `value` is two-way.

components.name: check-box
components.description: A checkbox with a label and an optional description, on a native <input type="checkbox">: it submits `value` under its `name` when checked, takes `required`, and the whole label is the target. `indeterminate` shows the mixed state (for a "select all" over a partial selection). `checked` is two-way.

components.name: radio-group
components.description: A set of options where one is chosen, on native radio buttons in a <fieldset>: arrow keys move between them, the choice submits under `name`, and `required` validates. `options` is `[{ value, label, description? }]`; `value` is two-way. `orientation="horizontal"` puts them in a row.

components.name: select-field
components.description: A labelled dropdown on a native <select>: the platform's own picker on every device, keyboard typeahead, autofill, and form submission under `name`. `options` is `[{ value, label }]`, or groups `[{ label, options: [...] }]`. `placeholder` adds an empty first choice, and with `required` the form won't submit until one is chosen. `value` is two-way.

components.name: status-badge
components.description: A small label for a status, a count or a category. `variant` is neutral, primary, success, warning, danger or outline; `dot` adds a coloured dot before the text. The colour is never the only signal: the text says it.

components.name: user-avatar
components.description: A person's picture, or their initials when there's no picture or it fails to load. `name` is the picture's text alternative (and where the initials come from). `size` is sm, md, lg or xl. `status` (online, away, busy, offline) adds a dot, and says so in words for screen readers.

components.name: content-card
components.description: A card: a picture, a heading, text and a footer, each optional. With `href` the heading is a link and the whole card is the target (one link for screen readers and the keyboard, not one per part), and buttons in the footer still work on their own.

components.name: alert-banner
components.description: A message in the page: info, success, warning or danger, with an icon, a heading and text. A danger alert is announced as soon as it appears (role="alert"); the others politely (role="status"). `dismissible` adds a close button, which hides it and fires `close`.

components.name: loading-spinner
components.description: Something is loading. Announced to screen readers once, as `label` ("Loading" by default), and shown as a ring that turns (a pulse instead, for visitors who asked for less motion). `size` is sm, md or lg; `inline` puts the label beside it.

components.name: skeleton-block
components.description: A grey placeholder in the shape of content that's on its way, so the page doesn't jump when it arrives. `shape` is text (`lines` lines, the last one shorter), circle or rect; `width` and `height` take any CSS length. Hidden from screen readers: say "loading" once elsewhere (a loading-spinner, or `aria-busy` on the region being filled).

components.name: toast-region
components.description: Short notifications that appear in a corner and go away by themselves. Put one region on the page; anything (a framework, a plain script) shows a toast by dispatching an event, so nothing needs a reference to it: `document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('toast', { detail: { message: 'Saved', variant: 'success' } }))`. `detail` takes `message`, `heading`, `variant` (info, success, warning, danger), `duration` in ms (0 keeps it until closed) and `action: { label, href }`. Toasts are announced politely (an error assertively), wait while hovered or focused, and sit above dialogs (the top layer).

components.name: backdrop-pattern
components.description: A decorative background behind its content: a grid, dots, a soft gradient mesh, film grain, or an aurora. Drawn in CSS from the theme's colours, so it follows light, dark and any theme. It's hidden from screen readers and never takes clicks or focus; with `animated` the mesh and aurora drift slowly, and stay still for visitors who asked for less motion. `fade` softens the edges toward the page. `size` is the grid or dot spacing.

components.name: switcher-layout
components.description: Children side by side in equal columns while the container is wide enough, and stacked one above the other below `threshold` (the container's width, not the screen's, so it works in a sidebar as well as the page). More than `limit` children always stack. Every child switches at once: no awkward row of two over one.

components.name: reel-layout
components.description: A row that scrolls sideways: cards, photos, episodes. Each child is `item` wide and snaps into place. The row is a labelled region that takes focus, so arrow keys scroll it; `controls` adds previous and next buttons that move one item at a time, and are disabled at either end.
